title: Exploring a shared registry opportunity with Canadian MPS Society

sentences.text: At National MPS Society, we support families affected by MPS II (Hunter syndrome); Canadian MPS Society supports families affected by MPS I.
Both conditions involve missing enzyme activity and a buildup of heparan and dermatan sulfate, although the enzymes differ.
The atlas also infers similar symptom patterns, but its confidence is 0.49—below 0.5—so this is a starting point for discussion, not proof that our communities have identical needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II Natural History and the Registry of Patients Diagnosed With Lysosomal Storage Diseases already include people with MPS II.
We could begin by comparing what these resources collect, rather than proposing a new registry.
The atlas lists Canadian MPS Registry as including MPS I, but its quoted source discusses newborn screening rather than registry participation, so that claim needs confirmation.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: We should preserve the distinction between the enzyme affected in MPS II, iduronate-2-sulfatase, and the enzyme affected in MPS I, alpha-L-iduronidase.

Please help us check whether decreased iduronate sulfatase level, tracheobronchomalacia and intestinal pseudo-obstruction also occur in MPS I, rather than treating gaps in the atlas as confirmed differences.
Before any sharing, let us confirm registry eligibility and which information could meaningfully be compared.

This month, I propose sending Canadian MPS Society one focused inquiry asking whether Canadian MPS Registry could include people with IDS-related MPS II, and requesting confirmation of its current scope.
No open questions are recorded yet in the supplied atlas.
I am writing on behalf of National MPS Society to explore a small collaboration.
Our MPS II community and the MPS I families you support share enzyme-deficiency and storage-related biology.
Could you confirm Canadian MPS Registry's scope and whether it could include MPS II?
We would welcome your guidance before taking this further.
[Your name], on behalf of National MPS Society
